title: A Puff of Air

patient.name: Mdm Ong Siew Hong
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine non-contact tonometry — focus on correct technique

history.hpc: Mdm Ong says 'I scared of the air puff, will it pain?' She wears glasses and is a little nervous about the test. This station focuses on performing NCT correctly and putting her at ease.
history.pmhx: No eye problems. Wears glasses. No drug allergies.

examination_findings.fundus: Not the focus of this station

investigations.task: Perform non-contact tonometry with correct technique and infection control, and record the readings
investigations.key_points: Hand hygiene; wipe machine contact parts before and after; remove glasses/contact lenses; explain the air puff; position comfortably; right eye first; record both in mmHg

diagnosis: Non-contact tonometry is performed correctly: hand hygiene and wiping of machine contact parts, removing glasses, explaining the air puff to reassure the patient, testing the right eye first, and recording both readings in mmHg (15/16, within the normal 10–21 mmHg range). This is a procedural/technique station.

immediate: Confirm identity and perform hand hygiene
Wipe the machine parts that contact the patient with alcohol wipes before starting
Ask the patient to remove glasses or contact lenses
Reassure her and explain that a puff of air will be blown into each eye, and it does not hurt
Position the patient comfortably at the machine
Perform NCT right eye first, then left, and record both readings in mmHg
Wipe machine contact parts and perform hand hygiene afterwards; document the readings
follow_up: Flag to the doctor if the readings are outside the normal range
Repeat if a reading seems unreliable
patient_education: Reassure that the air puff is quick and painless
Explain why glasses must be removed for the test
Explain the readings will be reviewed by the doctor

key_points: Confirms identity and explains the test to reassure the patient
Asks the patient to remove glasses/contact lenses
Gains cooperation from an anxious patient
Performs hand hygiene and wipes machine contact parts before and after
Knows the normal IOP range (~10–21 mmHg)
Understands the air-puff principle of NCT
Knows to test the right eye first by convention
Knows readings outside normal need flagging
